hints: Look at P first. It is the new single strand peeling away from the DNA inside the RNA polymerase bubble. Ask yourself if this fresh RNA in an animal nucleus is already finished.

Now look at Q and R. Only one DNA strand (Q) is base-pairing with P inside the bubble. Recall which two names mean the strand that is actually read, and what we call the other strand that is not read.
walkthrough:
**Identify P, the new RNA strand**

P is the single-stranded RNA molecule being made and released by RNA polymerase.

In the nucleus of an animal cell, this first product still contains both introns and exons. It has not yet been spliced, so it is called the primary transcript (pre-mRNA), not mature mRNA.

**Identify Q and R, the two DNA strands**

Inside the bubble, strand Q is unwound and base-paired with the new RNA P. That means Q is the strand being read.

The strand being read has two equivalent names: template strand = transcribed strand. Strand R is not being read, so it is the non-transcribed strand (also called the coding strand).

**Match to the table**

We need P = primary transcript, Q = template strand (which is the transcribed strand), R = non-transcribed strand.

Only row D gives all three correctly.

options.A: Incorrect because P is not yet mature mRNA, and Q and R are swapped. Q is the strand being read, not R.
options.B: P is correctly called primary transcript, but Q and R are swapped. Q is the template (transcribed) strand, not R.
options.C: Q and R are correct, but P is wrong. The unspliced RNA made in the nucleus is a primary transcript, not finished mRNA.
options.D: Correct. P is the primary transcript, Q is the template strand (same as transcribed strand), and R is the non-transcribed strand.
